text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING (sev2) - Canary latency surge observed after canary deploy 2026-03-15T10:42Z. Alerts from runtime: increased p99 and kernel-fallback counts. Please acknowledge.

maya: ack. seeing p50 ~120ms, p95 ~800ms -> p99 spiking to 2.6s for canary slice. throughput per-host dropped ~30% since deploy. root deploy id=deploy-2026-03-15-12:40, canary slice=canary-7

sam: on it. which flag/commit was in the canary? any obvious kernel fallback traces?

maya: canary enabled new prefetch aggro: `runtime.prefetch_strategy=v2` + batching changes: `batcher.max_batch_delay_ms=15`.

nate: logs show repeated kernel fallback logs on host gpu-46: `kernel_fallback=true` and many `enqueue_batch timeout` entries.

lee: observed KV cache thrash too; eviction rate doubled during spike. suspect prefetch + smaller batch window caused more concurrency and fallback to slower kernel path.

ops_lead: tagging customer-impact. @darya can you check top customers on canary route? run quick query on router logs.

darya: quick check: 3 high-traffic customers have elevated error rate (5xx) and p99 >2s. No broad 5xx spike, mostly increased tail latency and some timeouts in upstreams. I'll DM account owners.

maya: stack traces attached in logs channel: snippet shows kernel selection falling back at sequence_len > 1024 after prefetch burst.

sre-bot: Auto-detection: rate-limit of batcher reached on canary hosts -> falling back to single-thread path. See runbook: https://redwood/internal/runbooks/runtime-kernel-fallback

sam: plan: 1) disable prefetch strategy on canary (kill-switch) 2) if no improvement, rollback canary to previous deploy 3) notify customers and escalate.

nate: how do we flip the kill-switch? feature flag service or config push?

maya: can flip via runtime feature flags service. command (devops creds):

```
# disable new prefetch for canary route
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN" \
  https://flags.redwood/api/v1/flags/runtime.prefetch_strategy -d '{"value":"v1","scope":"canary-7"}'
```

maya: I can run it now if ops_lead gives go.

ops_lead: do it. also increase batch delay to 50ms temporarily to reduce enqueue churn.

maya: toggled flag -> response 200. bumping `batcher.max_batch_delay_ms` to 50 on canary via deploy agent now:

```
rctl update-config --slice canary-7 --set batcher.max_batch_delay_ms=50
```

sre-bot: CONFIG-UPDATE: batcher.max_batch_delay_ms updated for canary-7. Monitoring for 2 minutes.

lee: initial metrics after 90s: p99 dropped from 2.6s -> 1.1s, kernel_fallback events reduced ~75%, throughput recovering to ~92% of baseline.

darya: customer impact note: one customer reported a degraded search experience for ~10 minutes, no data loss. Accounts notified.

sam: good. keep canary running 15m with new settings; if stable we can promote or do a controlled rollout with smaller batch window and additional limits.

nate: I'm preparing a rollback path just in case. Command to rollback canary to previous stable:

```
rdeploy rollback --deploy-id deploy-2026-03-15-12:40 --target canary-7
```

maya: agree hold for 15m. if any 5xx >1% or p99 >1.5s -> we rollback.

ops_lead: also add a temporary auto-fallback rule: if kernel_fallback_count > 50/min -> route 100% of canary traffic to stable.

sre-bot: Alert rule created: `canary-7-kernel-fallback-watch` threshold 50/min, action=route-to-stable.

lee: after 12m stable, p99 roughly 350ms, throughput back to 98%. no further 5xx spikes.

maya: handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. Passing to night oncall @sam. Ops lead please confirm escalation doc and postmortem owner.

ops_lead: I'll own the postmortem. Sam takes oncall handoff. Nate/Lee/Darya on follow-ups for rollout safety checks and producer tests.

sam: taking handoff. summary: canary deployed with prefetch v2 + lower batch delay -> caused kernel fallback and batching thrash -> toggled prefetch to v1 and increased delay -> mitigated. Next actions: add canary-level safety limits, add kernel-fallback circuit-breaker, add pre-deploy synthetic that exercises high-seq lengths.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: canary stabilized after kill-switch and config adjustments. Severity downgraded to sev3 at 2959876610.

maya: thanks team. postmortem link will be created by ops_lead. I'll attach logs and metrics snapshots.

ops_lead: creating postmortem doc: https://redwood/internal/postmortems/2959876543-canary-prefetch-regression

sre-bot: handoff note: paging cleared. on-call: sam. escalation channel reserved for 1hr.

sam: acknowledging handoff. leaving a few checks for next shift: 1) ensure auto-fallback rule didn't route any stable traffic during tests, 2) verify canary promotion won't re-enable prefetch v2 without safety gates.

darya: customer follow-ups sent. will update postmortem with account impact summary.

maya: closing thread once postmortem link has initial draft.
